```{python}
import polars as pl 
import numpy as np
from lets_plot import *
import polars.selectors as cs
# add the additional libraries you need to import for ML here

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```

```{python}
# Read in star wars data:
df = pl.read_csv('https://byuidatascience.github.io/DS250-Course-Polars/Data/StarWars_with_emails.csv', skip_rows=10) #in this case skip_lines does the same
```

```{python}
df = df.filter((pl.col('Household Income') != 'Response') | (pl.col('Household Income').is_null()))
```

```{python}
# Get counts of the number range variables:
display(df.group_by('Household Income').agg(pl.len()))
display(df.group_by('Age').agg(pl.len()))
```

### How would you convert this?

```{python}
new_df = df.with_columns(pl.col(
    'Household Income').str.replace_all(r',', '').str.extract(r'^\$([\d,]+)').cast(pl.Int32).alias('income')
).group_by('income').agg(pl.len())

# new_df['income'].max() # the max value is 150,000
# So I could cast it to a int32
```

## Ordinal categories

```{python}
with pl.Config(tbl_width_chars=100):
    display(df.group_by('Education').agg(pl.len()))
```

```{python}
df.with_columns(pl.col('Education').replace_strict(
    {
        "Less than high school degree": 1,
        "High school degree": 2,
        "Some college or Associate degree": 3,
        "Bachelor degree": 4,
        "Graduate degree": 5
    }
)).group_by('Education').agg(pl.len())

```

## Let’s look at favorability rating. 

```{python}
df.group_by('Please state whether you view the following characters favorably, unfavorably, or are unfamiliar with him/her.').agg(pl.len())
```

```{python}
df.to_dummies('Gender').agg(pl.len()) # there were only 3 options in gender, male, female, and null. This will create 3 columns.
```

```{python}
display(df.select('Gender'))
df.to_dummies('Gender').select(pl.col(r'^Gender.*$'))
```
